title: True is His court
hook: true is the Lord, true His court, true His works (Sukhmani 17)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the salok of ashtpadi 17, sach, and your line: true then, true now. Did aad sach steady you when something shifted? Today the stanzas take that truth and run it through everything. Day five hundred three.

The cashier is busy and distracted, and she hands you change for a fifty when you gave her a twenty. Nobody saw. The store is a big chain; it won't miss thirty dollars. You're halfway to the door. It's a small pause: the moment where the truth costs something and nobody would ever know. The seventeenth ashtpadi has an answer for that pause, and it isn't a rule. It's a description of what the world is made of. Today: true is His court.
screen: `CHANGE FOR A FIFTY, NOT A TWENTY.` → `NOBODY SAW.` → `HALFWAY TO THE DOOR.`

segments.voice: After yesterday's salok, the first stanza of the seventeenth ashtpadi is built almost entirely out of one word, repeated: sat. True. In paraphrase: true are His feet, and true the one who touches them. True His worship, true the one who serves. True His sight, true the one who sees. True His Name, true the one who remembers it. True the Word, and true the One who speaks it. Line after line, sat, sat, sat, until the truth isn't a single fact anymore but the material everything is made of. Today's title adds an image from elsewhere in Gurbani: the dargah. Dargah is a Persian word for a royal court, the place where a ruler sits and cases are heard. In Gurbani, the dargah is God's court, where every life is finally seen as it really was. And Gurbani calls it the sachee dargah: the true court. Not a court where the clever win, or the rich, or the well-connected. A court where only what's real counts. Put those together and you see what the ashtpadi is doing. If the One is true, and the court is true, and the works are true, and the Word is true, then truth isn't one rule among many. It's the grain of the wood. A lie isn't just breaking a rule; it's cutting against the grain of everything. Read that way, the cashier moment changes. The question stops being, will anyone know? In the ashtpadi's picture of a world that's true all through, the thirty dollars is already known, not by a camera, but by the way things are. Handing it back isn't heroic. It's going with the grain.
screen: `SAT, SAT, SAT: LINE AFTER LINE.` · `DARGAH: THE ROYAL COURT.` · `THE TRUE COURT, WHERE ONLY THE REAL COUNTS.` · `TRUTH IS THE GRAIN OF THE WOOD.` · then, large: `TRUE ALL THROUGH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: be true in one small thing, starting here. Sit and ask yourself one honest question, gently: is there one small place in my life where I've been a little untrue? An excuse, an exaggeration, a thing left unsaid. Don't judge it. Just see it, the way it really is. Then picture the small true step: the correction, the plain answer, the change handed back. Rest with that picture for the rest of the sit. The bell holds the time.
Dargah, a court. The sachee dargah, where only what's real counts; in the seventeenth ashtpadi, everything about the One is sat, true, through and through.
Your line: true all through. Today, be true in one small thing that nobody would ever check: the exact time, the real reason, the correct change. Day five hundred three.

howItsDone: Sikhs reciting Sukhmani Sahib's seventeenth ashtpadi repeat sat, true, through line after line, and Gurbani speaks of the sachee dargah, God's true court, where each life is seen as it really was.

original.note: Gurmukhi: dargah, a court; in Gurbani, God's court. From Persian.

trapdoor: what you thought: God's court is a final exam after death.
what it means: truth is what everything is made of, so every small moment is already known for what it is.
what a scholar hears: Gurbani borrows dargah and darbar from Persian court language, and the stanza's sat, sat pairings join each true thing with the one who meets it.

sources.ref: Sukhmani Sahib, ashtpadi 17, stanza 1 (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 285)

notes: Ashtpadi 17 stanza 1 paraphrased: charan sat sat parsanhaar; poojaa sat sat sevdaar; darsan sat sat pekhanhaar; naam sat sat dhiaavanhaar; sabad sat sat prabh baktaa; surat sat sat jas suntaa. Confirm.
The word dargah may not appear in this ashtpadi; the outline's 'true His court' is taught via Gurbani's common phrase sachee dargah. A Keeper should confirm or adjust.
